intended_object: An infinite path in a leveled DAG (as in a run DAG of an alternating Büchi automaton): a sequence of states q_0, q_1, … together with a starting level n such that for every i there is an edge from (q_i, n+i) to (q_{i+1}, n+i+1). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `RunDAG.accepting`.
explanation:
In this file an edge is stored as a pair ((q, i), q'), meaning the edge (q, i) → (q', i+1); `edge_closure` guarantees that both endpoints are in V. The definition asks for a starting level n such that, for every i, ((p i, n+i), p (i+1)) ∈ E. So consecutive states of p are joined by edges that move up one level at a time, starting at level n. That is exactly an infinite path that may start at any level, as the docstring says.

This matches the standard definition of an accepting run DAG (Kupferman–Vardi), which quantifies over every infinite path of the DAG and not only those starting at the root. Its use in `RunDAG.accepting` ("every path visits F infinitely often") is the standard Büchi acceptance condition.

The definition is not too narrow. The leveled structure over ℕ is the whole content of this DAG notion, and Q is an arbitrary type. Mathlib has no notion of infinite paths in such leveled DAGs, so there is no `mathlib_counterpart`.
